commentary_text:
[P01] The archive from Brookside Training Oval is less a conventional highlights reel than a stitched record of how the match was scored. Tidehaven chose to bat, and the first pictures are from the end-on camera while the television graphics computer was still taking its feed from a trainee's console. Harvey Lane defended the first legal ball from Noah Vance and lost his stumps to the next. A crowd microphone briefly obscured the umpire's signal, but both the paper book and the bowler-end counter identify the dismissal as delivery TV-001-B. Rohan Blake then walked in, and a delayed square-leg clip arrived before the live camera had caught up.

[P02] That delayed clip showed Blake and Miles Sharp crossing, and the trainee first treated the movement as a completed run. The umpire log attached the picture to TV-001-C, however, a ball already coded wide before either batter set off; the team event survives but no batter owns the movement. Sharp was bowled on the next legal delivery, TV-002-A. The paper book marks the side at one with two batters gone, while the television ribbon briefly carried a higher figure because it had both the wide and the running picture. The scorer did not issue a replacement total; she merely linked both pictures to the same delivery signature.

[P03] Nolan Reed joined Blake and spent his first few balls pinned behind the crease. Blake drove Vance through cover in the live feed, then worked separate deliveries into the leg side and behind point. A second cover-drive clip appeared during a drinks promo, with the same sightscreen attendant crossing the frame and the same deep fielder slipping as in the live shot. The archive editor labelled it REPLAY-A rather than a new ball. At the other end Nolan eventually completed one run. The partnership monitor was still provisional, because one tight-angle running clip had no visible umpire and another reverse angle lacked the broadcast clock.

[P04] Arlo Finch, keeping for Ridgefield, supplied the decisive identity clue from behind the stumps. His helmet-camera file carried the ball-change code used before the drinks promo, placing the tight-angle clip on TV-001-C, the wide already discussed, rather than in the Blake-Nolan stand. The reverse-angle picture was matched to Blake's behind-point single by the non-striker's distinctive bat tape and the same return throw. Those matches changed ownership and duplication status across the batter and partnership views without creating a new team event. The remaining Blake scoring pictures have separate delivery identifiers, while Nolan's completed run and the stand's lone extra are independently marked in the paper book.

[P05] The score ribbon next settled at eleven when Finch held Blake from Vance at 5.4. That caption is retained in the archive because its event time agrees with the umpire card, not because the later programme repeated it. Nolan and Caleb Frost then occupied the crease through a quiet passage. A leg-side delivery called wide was displayed twice, once live and once inside an analysis box, but the replay carries the same NV-05-W signature. Nolan was bowled at 7.3. The paper scorer's next-state line shows twelve at the fourth wicket, giving the later partnership material a clean boundary even though the television crawl had temporarily counted the analysis-box copy.

[P06] Caleb and Owen Marsh began with the surface looking slower by the minute. Owen's square drive was the only boundary in their stand, and a later clip shows him turning the strike over. That single was transmitted again after a camera reset; the archive clock, striker's glove adjustment and return path all match the original. Caleb's early push was initially entered as a batter run, but the umpire's coded card says the ball brushed his pad and that the completed run belongs in the leg-bye channel. That ruling is referenced by delivery AW-08-C; nowhere on the card does the official state either man's innings aggregate.

[P07] The next over contained a cluster that explains why the live graphics never looked stable. Arjun Wells sent a ball beyond Owen's reach, and the square-leg console created one wide event. A near-identical clip from the following over arrived with the old camera timestamp and was provisionally accepted as another. The central scorer later paired it with the first by ball serial and fielder position. In between, Owen tucked a genuinely different delivery behind square and crossed. Caleb found one scoring stroke of his own after the pad incident. A dead-ball scamper also appeared on the trainee card, although the bowler had broken the stumps before the batters moved.

[P08] The dead-ball entry could not be resolved from the pictures alone. The authoritative source was the umpire log, which records AW-11-D as dead when the striker withdrew; the broadcast's apparent run belongs to no team, batter or stand ledger. The legitimate leg-side single has a separate sound spike and delivery serial. Owen was subsequently bowled by Wells on the second legal ball of the fourteenth over. The preceding fixed point was Nolan's dismissal many paragraphs earlier. Between those boundaries the archive contains the pad reclassification, a duplicated wide clip, one cancelled scamper and several valid scoring events, so no single local caption defines the stand.

[P09] Dylan Pierce was bowled later in the same Wells spell without the team score moving. A stump-camera package then replayed both Owen's and Dylan's dismissals under new video filenames. The production rundown, rather than a score caption, ties those files back to AW-13-B and AW-14-E. Caleb survived into the sixteenth over, where an appeal struck him in front. A side-on archive asset from that passage also appeared to show Caleb taking another pad contact and completing a run; with its clock strip missing, the secondary console kept it as a plausible new leg-bye candidate. Its identity was deferred rather than decided beside the earlier pad ruling.

[P10] Theo Grant made a single before the next wicket sequence. The television crawl initially left Theo's catch in Wells's column, an understandable continuation after the earlier bowled and lbw decisions. The scorer's dismissal slip instead identifies Elias Grant as the bowler and Ben Cole as catcher; the over stamp EG-17-C matches the live commentary call. The score had reached thirty by then. The distinction matters twice: Elias owns that catch, and Wells does not. Later compilations replay Theo's dismissal adjacent to the Caleb lbw, but the two event signatures and two bowlers remain separate in the official reconciliation.

[P11] Arun Cole and Kian Stone then nudged the innings onward. Four extras occurred in their stand, although the source cards do not package them as one tidy announcement: two separate wide signals appear on Ben Cole's spell sheet, and a paired signal in Wells's return spell is supported by two distinct ball serials. Arun completed two batter runs across different overs, Kian one, and the stand closed when Wells bowled Arun at 19.1. An overnight edit placed one of Ben's wide clips beside the Wells pair, but the bowler-end cards preserve three distinct delivery identities across those two bowlers.

[P12] Vikram Holt was last in. A Wells delivery passed the bat and drew a wide signal before the legal sequence resumed. The delayed highlights strip later replayed that same miss after the wicket and gave it a fresh asset number; matching advertising-board movement and the ball-retrieval path show it is the original event. Vikram was bowled after two earlier legal balls in that over. That was Tidehaven's tenth completed dismissal. No batter run was made in the final stand, although the wide and its replay occupied two broadcast slots.

[P13] During the interval the scorers compared the extras channels rather than announcing a replacement innings line. Vance's sheet contains two separate occasions on which consecutive wide signals belong to distinct balls, while Elias's has none. The original AW-08-C ruling remains in the leg-bye channel, but the clockless side-on pad asset from the later spell is still quarantined pending a production match. A Wells overstep carries its own no-ball code, and the keeper audit found no untouched-ball bye. The batter-event ledger and these extras channels must reconcile with every wicket-state boundary rather than treating the provisional pad asset as decisive.

[P14] The wicket audit was conducted independently. Vance's credit lines were checked against the early dismissal signatures, and Nolan's stump-camera close-up was collapsed with NV-07-C rather than treated as another wicket. Wells's candidate lines were checked across the later dismissal slips, with Theo retained under Elias after the over-stamp review. No run-out, obstruction or retired-out event appears in the innings. A separate wicket-state card attaches twenty-four to Owen's dismissal. Thus the dismissed batters can be mapped to bowler credits without relying on the briefly incorrect scrolling columns.

[P15] Ridgefield's chase began under brighter light, but its feed was no cleaner. Owen Marsh's opening ball was called no-ball after Arlo Finch drove in the air and was caught. The front-on replay and the umpire card share OM-00-A, so the catch, the overstep and the running pictures are facets of one event, not separate deliveries. Finch remained at the crease. The broadcast then repeated the catch twice while analysts discussed the call. Neither replay has a legal-ball tick, and neither can create a dismissal, though the delivery's no-ball value remains in the team and bowler ledgers.

[P16] Finch responded with a cover boundary on a legal ball, and another four came through midwicket later in the over. Ben Cole struck a six during the opening stand. Owen also sent two balls beyond Finch's reach during the spell; the signals belong to different deliveries. When an attempted catch off Finch appeared between them, the synchronized heel frame showed Owen had not overstepped on that occasion and the ball was recorded as a legal scoring shot rather than another no-ball. A regional replay altered the clip order, so chronological position alone could not settle batter ownership.

[P17] Ben's wicket arrived near the end of Owen's second over. He drove a legal delivery toward Blake, who held it. The dismissal card carries OM-02-F, distinct from the opening no-ball catch of Finch, and later close-ups of Blake's hands retain the same code. The ground ribbon showed eighteen with one wicket down when the catch was confirmed. The opening partnership also contains the delivery extra from OM-00-A. Finch's opening contribution is not stated on any final batter graphic; it must agree with the wicket-state figure, Ben's accepted event set and that delivery extra.

[P18] Noah Vance joined Finch, and Arun Cole began the next over with a sequence of leg-side misses. The umpire card recognizes three different wide events before a legal dot; the television cut the first miss into both a live shot and a slow-motion insert. Another pair of misses later in the over have distinct ball serials despite looking nearly identical. A graphic operator also marked a heel-near-line delivery as a possible overstep. The ordinary broadcast angle cannot settle the call, and the temporary extras ribbon retains that candidate while the synchronized frame list is requested from the technical archive.

[P19] Finch drove one legal Arun ball through extra cover, then a replay of his earlier opening boundary appeared immediately afterward. The second clip has the old OM camera code and cannot be part of the new stand. Noah opened his account with a single, and later completed another. A running picture that seemed to give Finch one more was linked by shirt movement and the umpire's arm to Arun's final wide, so it remains a team extra rather than a batter run. The stand tracker was therefore carrying two locally plausible versions while the video identities were unresolved.

[P20] Caleb Frost took the ball for the closing over. His first broadcast slot showed an apparent legal delivery and a scrambled run, but the umpire card marks CF-04-A as an overstep. The run was completed from Finch's bat and the no-ball value also belongs to the innings, while the delivery does not advance the legal-ball counter. A later wide-looking replay was actually the earlier Arun event, recognizable from the bowler's sleeve and the east-stand shadow. Caleb's remaining deliveries were legal. Finch and Noah exchanged the strike without another dismissal.

[P21] With two legal balls of the fourth over completed, the paper book says Ridgefield had drawn level with Tidehaven's terminal run state. The broadcast ribbon was temporarily four higher because it had appended the replayed opening cover drive from P19. The archive controller removed that asset after matching its OM code, but issued no fresh score caption. On the next legal ball Finch completed the winning single. The ball counter therefore stops on the third legal delivery of that over, while the cancelled opening catch and Caleb's overstep had occupied broadcast time without advancing that counter.

[P22] The chase reconciliation was split among three desks. The legal-ball clerk places OM-02-F on the fifth counted delivery of Owen's second over, while the production desk links the later close-ups of Blake's hands to that same catch asset. Arun's wide signals remain on a separate sheet, and the unresolved heel frame is sent onward without a local ruling. A downstream ticker mixed several replay assets into its columns, so neither its wicket entry nor its extras entry is treated as authoritative. The desks retain event identifiers and postpone their final cross-ledger reconciliation.

[P23] The partnership desk retained its opening state from the earlier catch but did not close the record until the later legal-ball audit in P28. Inside that interval, Noah's two separate singles are supported by legal-ball ticks. Finch's valid contribution contains the extra-cover boundary, other distinct scoring shots and the winning single, but excludes the old opening replay and the run picture assigned to an Arun wide. The stand also inherits Arun's recognized wides and Caleb's no-ball. Two provisional stand cards remain plausible until those ownership decisions are combined with the start and end states.

[P24] A separate batter audit followed Finch across both stands. In the opening phase, the wicket-state figure must be partitioned among Ben's accepted scoring events, the opening delivery extra and Finch's legal shots; the cancelled catch contributes no dismissal or batter loss. Ben's crossed run is supported by its own ball serial despite appearing out of sequence in the regional package. In the later phase, Noah's two legal singles and the accepted extras are separated from Finch's shots. The opening cover replay cannot cross the partnership boundary merely because it was broadcast during the second stand. The two phase records share a player but not an event.

[P25] The archivist then compared team conservation in both innings. For Tidehaven, the accepted batter accounts sum to twenty-two: the non-target batters contribute no run from Lane, Sharp, Dylan or Vikram, one each from Nolan, Theo and Kian, two each from Caleb and Arun, with Blake and Owen determined by their corrected event sets. An interval signature audit also retains Owen's remaining earlier single as distinct from the two already discussed. For Ridgefield, Ben and Noah supply their accepted batter events, Finch supplies the disjoint phase records, and all other listed batters never appeared. The chase extras are exhausted by recognized wides and oversteps.

[P26] The partnership conservation sheet offers another view of Tidehaven without printing a final card. The first four stands move the wicket states from the opening dismissal through Nolan's wicket. The Caleb-Owen stand spans the fixed states in P05 and P14. Wells's own sheet preserves three paired wide occasions after the old camera duplicate is resolved. The production manifest now matches the clockless pad asset from P09 to AW-08-C by ball scuff, keeper crouch and return path, so it is a second view of the earlier event rather than a later team run. Arun's dismissal fixes the side on thirty-five, and every stand boundary remains tied to one dismissal event.

[P27] Legal-ball accounting supplies the last independent constraint on Tidehaven. Vance delivered six complete overs, Wells nine overs and three legal balls, Elias two complete overs, and Ben three. Wides and the Wells no-ball did not increase the legal count. The last wicket is attached to Wells's third legal ball after the twentieth over, consistent with the innings closure in P12. The television asset count is larger because it includes repeated wides and replayed wickets, but asset count is never substituted for balls faced or overs bowled.

[P28] Ridgefield's legal-ball account works similarly. Owen's two completed overs contain more broadcast slots than counted deliveries because the opening sequence includes an umpire-coded irregular ball. Arun delivered a complete over. Caleb's closing sequence begins with an uncounted overstep and is followed by three legal balls, and those logs confirm the terminal event described in P21. The technical asset total is larger than the ball counter, so the reconciliation depends on delivery identities rather than clip count.

[P29] The source hierarchy remained stable throughout the reconstruction. Umpire cards decide legality and extras class; the paper scorer decides batter and partnership ownership after consulting those cards; production manifests decide whether two video assets represent one delivery; the live television ribbon is only provisional. The synchronized heel sequence requested in P18 places Arun's back foot behind the line on AC-03-D, and the legal-ball clerk's continuous count accepts that frame match. Elsewhere, TV-001-C resolves Blake's apparent run and the AW-08-C media pair resolves Caleb's pad ownership. Their consequences propagate through several ledgers.

[P30] The match result itself provides a broad check rather than a shortcut. Ridgefield won with nine wickets standing after chasing one more than Tidehaven made. That statement fixes the relationship between the innings, but not the component values, because the archive still requires the legal-ball endpoint, the solitary valid chase dismissal and the removal of duplicated scoring footage. Likewise, Noah Vance's player-of-the-match citation does not state his bowling column; his credits must be recovered from the distinct early dismissal signatures and the Nolan replay match.

[P31] Before sealing the archive, the scorer ran one more collision check on similar-looking events. Blake's two cover clips were one shot shown twice, whereas Finch's cover and midwicket boundaries in the opening phase were distinct. The later close-ups of Ben's catch all retain OM-02-F and collapse into the live dismissal asset. Wells's wickets of Owen and Dylan had adjacent replay filenames yet separate over stamps. The clockless Caleb pad view, by contrast, carries the same ball scuff and keeper movement as AW-08-C. These identity decisions prevent both silent duplication and mistaken cancellation.

[P32] The retained record is therefore an event graph rather than a polished score announcement. Dismissal nodes establish nonlocal state boundaries; legality nodes govern extras, wicket credit and ball counts; ownership nodes partition team events among batters and partnerships; replay links collapse duplicate media assets. Tidehaven's fifth-wicket boundary and Ridgefield's sole wicket boundary connect the innings-level, batter, bowling and partnership views. A reader can reconstruct every requested scalar and the formatted terminal states from those links, but no final target cell is spoken as a standalone result in the commentary.
